title: Compliance for Everyone
description: What compliance really means, why the rules exist, and how they are used day to day, told three ways: crack a case, make the calls yourself, then play it through.
audience: Anyone starting a job where rules matter, no legal background needed.

chapters.title: Highlights
chapters.summary: What this lesson covers, one card at a time: the rules, where they come from, and why they are worth following.

chapters.title: The Marigold Kitchen Case
chapters.summary: Fourteen people fell ill after a catered lunch. Investigate the kitchen, question the staff and discover what compliance is by finding out what went wrong.

chapters.title: A Week at BrightPath
chapters.summary: You are the new coordinator at a tutoring company. Ten real decisions about data, safety, gifts and records, each explained whichever way you choose.

chapters.title: Compliance Cove
chapters.summary: A playable island tour that consolidates the ideas: rules, training, audits, speaking up and culture, ending with inspection day.

objectives: Explain what compliance is and who writes the rules an organisation follows
Spot the everyday moments where a rule applies: data, gifts, safety, records
Describe what training, audits and speaking up are actually for
Choose the compliant action in a realistic situation and say why
prerequisites: None. Everyday work experience is enough

glossary.definition: Doing what the rules that apply to your work require, and being able to show that you did.
A rule written by a government agency under a law, with the force of law behind it.
A rule an organisation writes for itself, often to meet a law or standard in its own way.
A planned check that the rules are being followed, using records and observation, by someone not doing the work.
Written evidence that a required check or action happened, when, and by whom.
Reporting a concern about a rule being broken through a channel the organisation protects.
What people do when nobody is checking; the habits that make rules work or fail.
